final_analysis.summary: Index Lemma framework does not discriminate sub vs at-threshold cycles in our setting.

trivial_invariants_found.B[mover_in_triangle][signed_mono0]: ≡ 0 in 100% of records (sub AND at). Closed 2-torus ⟹ content = 0 trivially. No discriminating bite.

marginal_statistical_shifts.B[nonzero][signed_mono0] at n=7, L=18: sub frac_zero=0.78 vs at frac_zero=0.56; ~22 pp shift but non-zero values appear in BOTH regimes. Not forced.

final_analysis.verdict_reason: 1. Trivially-forced invariants (B[mover_in_triangle]) are identical in both regimes (always 0). 2. Non-trivial signed contents (B[high], C[sourcebinary] T_signed) concentrate at 0 in BOTH regimes with similar frequencies, differing only in tail density. 3. Mode mismatches (12 out of 52 signed-content stats) differ by ±1 and are sample-noise. 4. Strongest signals (B[nonzero] at n=8) are L-dependent sampling artifacts: the simple DFS enumerator finds mostly 'sweep-like' cycles at large L, which happen to have signed_mono0 ≡ -1 for at-threshold multisets but 0 for sub-threshold. This reflects a cycle-shape correlation, not a topological obstruction. 5. Book framework (M = Ch^N σ, subdivided n-simplex with proper (n+1)-coloring) fundamentally does not fit our setting: our good cycles are 1-dimensional closed loops in ∏ Z_{m_p}, and any 2-complex lift has no boundary (closed torus). Index Lemma identity C(M,c) = (-1)^i I_i(M,c) with ∂M = ∅ FORCES content = 0, so any non-trivial signed count we compute is a non-index-lemma quantity disguised as one.
final_analysis.conclusion: The Index Lemma is the book's tool for asynchronous shared-memory impossibility; it derives content ≠ 0 from symmetry + binomial common factors (Fact 12.5.4) on a subdivided n-simplex with rank-symmetric binary coloring. Our self-stabilization ring setting lacks the three structural ingredients: (1) simplex-subdivision cell structure, (2) an n-simplex boundary to inherit coloring from, (3) a symmetry group acting on the coloring. The closest analog we can construct is a closed 2-torus (position × cycle-step) on which content is trivially 0. Non-trivial statistical shifts observed (e.g., B[nonzero] at n=8) are sample-dependent cycle-shape biases, not topological invariants. Last binary discriminator confirmed DEAD.
